Issued at 201 AM EDT Thu Sep 10 2026

Today-Tonight...Strong mid/upper level ridging over the Carolinas
moves eastward today. Meanwhile the Atlantic ridge axis begins to
organize off of the Florida east coast. Prior to sunrise, a few
showers are present over the local Atlantic waters, moving NE
towards the coast. Most of this activity is weakening as it
approaches the more stable land mass of the peninsula. However, a
few showers will remain possible along the coast into the early
morning hours.

Light onshore flow this morning becomes SE this afternoon as the 
sea breeze develops, but remains under 10 mph. Deep moisture, with
PWATs 2.2-2.3"+, lingers over the peninsula today, with 50-60% 
coverage of showers and storms forecast once again. Convection is 
forecast to begin just inland from the coast by around 2 PM, then 
push into the interior through the afternoon, with a collision 
near the Orlando metro near to just after rush hour. Slightly 
lower PoPs for the coast (40-50%), with slow and erratic 
propagation persisting over the interior into the evening hours. A
few strong storms cannot be ruled out, mainly along the 
collision, with DCAPE near 800 J/kg. However, the main threat 
looks to be locally heavy rainfall due to slow moving storms, 
which could lead to minor flooding concerns. Showers and storms 
look to slowly diminish through the evening, with drier conditions
inland by midnight. A few showers or a storm will remain possible
along the Treasure Coast overnight.

High temperatures in the lower to mid-90s and high humidity will
lead to heat indices just below Heat Advisory criteria at 102-107
degrees. Be sure to stay hydrated and take frequent breaks if
spending time outside in the heat of the day. Overnight lows are
forecast to remain in the 70s.

Friday-Sunday...The Atlantic ridge strengthens Friday and into 
the weekend, as mid to upper level ridging moves off of the 
eastern seaboard. Meanwhile, the surface ridge axis establishes 
itself over the central Florida peninsula. Prevailing light 
southerly flow becomes SSE in the afternoons as the sea breeze 
develops and moves inland. Despite a slightly stronger east coast 
breeze, expect a collision over the interior each afternoon, with 
deep PWATs 2-2.3" supporting PoPs 60-70%. The mid- level ridge 
axis is forecast to be slightly farther south, producing light 
offshore steering flow. While a majority of storm propagation will
be erratic and slow, a drift towards the east coast through the 
evening hours will be possible. A few strong storms cannot be 
ruled out, with gusts near 50 mph, due to 500mb temperatures -7C 
and perhaps a small intrusion of Saharan Air Layer in the mid- 
levels. However, the main threat looks to be heavy rainfall from 
slow moving storms and deep moisture. Any slow moving storm will 
be capable of a quick 1-3" and could lead to minor flooding 
concerns, especially in areas that see multiple rounds.

Scattered showers and storms are forecast to linger into the
evening hours over the interior along the sea breeze collision.
Then, drier conditions develop for the overnight. But, onshore 
flow will maintain the chance for a few showers or a storm
(20-30%) along the Treasure Coast overnight and into the morning.
Highs in the lower 90s and muggy conditions will continue to
produce heat indices 102-107 degrees, just shy of Heat Advisory
criteria, while lows remain in the 70s.

Monday-Thursday...Strong ridging develops through the column next
week near the Carolinas, weakening the Atlantic ridge. This will
lead to strengthening onshore flow, perhaps even ENE at times,
around 10-15 mph. This wind regime would favor a dominant east
coast sea breeze and, in theory, lower coverage for the local CWA.
However, models differ on the amount of available moisture present
and how that will affect coverage of any onshore-moving showers 
and storms. Thus, the current forecast maintains near to slightly
above normal PoPs 40-70%. Onshore flow, breezy at times in the
afternoons, looks to keep high temperatures near normal in the
upper 80s to lower 90s. But, coastal areas are forecast to linger
in the upper 70s to near 80 overnight.
